cap: Delayed puberty is sorted by LH and FSH. High values mean the gonads failed, as in Turner or Klinefelter syndrome, and a karyotype is next. Low values mean the axis is quiet: constitutional delay is the most common cause, with a bone age about 2 years behind; low leptin suppresses GnRH pulses in thin athletes; Kallmann syndrome adds anosmia from failed GnRH neuron migration.
teach: In constitutional delay the bone age lags with puberty, so a low LH and FSH is appropriate for the bone age rather than a sign of GnRH deficiency; a healthy short boy with a late-maturing parent usually starts puberty on his own. Kallmann syndrome keeps LH low as the bone age advances and brings anosmia, sometimes with a cleft lip. Pubic hair can appear even when the gonads have failed, because adrenarche does not need them.
